Independently verified near-commanded flow, adequate inlet pressure, and absent cavitation vibration argue against pump problems. Agreement between temperature sensors, near-commanded flow, adequate pump inlet pressure, confirmed bypass closure, and steady process load weaken the alternatives.

The controlled test shows heat-transfer coefficient 39% below the clean reference at matched flow, supported by an elevated exchanger approach temperature. Independent position feedback confirms the commanded-closed bypass is closed. Near-commanded flow, adequate pump inlet pressure, absent cavitation vibration, agreeing temperature sensors, and steady load weaken the alternatives. The uncorroborated pump hum carries little diagnostic weight.

Exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite near-commanded flow. The deficit persists across stable loads. Independent bypass-position confirmation, agreeing temperature sensors, adequate pump inlet pressure, and absent cavitation-frequency vibration weaken the competing diagnoses. Fouling is strongly favored but has not been directly inspected.

The controlled test found a 39% reduction in heat-transfer coefficient at matched flow, strongly supporting exchanger fouling. Near-commanded flow, adequate inlet pressure, absent cavitation vibration, and normal motor current argue against pump cavitation. Independent confirmation of a closed bypass and agreement between temperature sensors weaken those alternatives. Steady load weakens a transient explanation.
